question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- Any $6\times 8$ matrix $A$ has at most $8$ distinct singular values
- Any $10\times 8$ matrix $A$ has at most $10$ distinct singular values.
- The matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]$ has two non-negative singular values.
question.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, since $A$ is a $6\times 8$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $8\times 6$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $8\times 8$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{8\times 6}\times {A}_{6\times 8}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{8\times 8}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $8$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is false. Since $A$ is a $10\times 8$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $8\times 10$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $8\times 8$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{8\times 10}\times {A}_{10\times 8}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{8\times 8}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $8$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is true.  Indeed, all singular values of any matrix are non-negative.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
